flags.text: Says the association is stronger for users with higher leader-directed affective polarization, 'particularly for participatory engagement'. The paper says it is 'often' stronger descriptively, that the moderation evidence is 'not uniform', and that the results are only 'partially consistent with Expectation 2' (p.13-14). The entry keeps the participation emphasis but drops the partial-support qualification.

key_findings.note: Within-person increases in online engagement followed by higher hostility; says the relationship is reciprocal ('suggesting', as the paper's 'may be reciprocal') but not that the reverse pattern is weaker.

scope_and_limits.note: Not causal (L2), may not generalize beyond X/Twitter (L1), Big Five controls do not test Dark Triad accounts (L6; 'not measured' is not said, but the Dark Triad part is). The quote for the causal part is NOT IN PAPER, but the entry has two faithful quotes, so it is credited. 'Does not generalize' is read as 'is not shown to generalize'; not flagged.

theoretical_positioning.note: Extending the revisionist view to online hostility is T2 and T3, but the only quote is spliced and marked NOT IN PAPER.

flags.text: Says the paper 'disputes the prior emphasis' that hostility is 'primarily explained' by grievance or personality. The paper 'does not seek to adjudicate between these literatures' (p.3) and says hostility is 'not only' associated with those explanations but also with engagement (p.15).
